title: Honey nut granola
description: Crunchy oven-baked granola with oats, nuts, seeds and honey. A big jar lasts two weeks.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Warm the honey and oil in a small pot on low heat until runny.
Chop the almonds and walnuts roughly. In a large bowl mix them with the oats, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds and cinnamon.
Pour the honey mix over and stir until everything is evenly coated.

steps.text: Spread it out on the tray in a thin layer and bake for 25 minutes, stirring once halfway, until golden.
steps.tip: Watch the edges near the end: they burn first. For big clusters, press it flat and do not stir.

steps.text: Stir in the cranberries and let it cool completely on the tray. It crisps up as it cools.
steps.tip: Kept in a closed jar, it stays crunchy for two weeks.

title: Chewy oat granola bars
description: No-fuss bars of oats, peanut butter, honey, raisins and seeds. Cut into 12 and wrap for lunch boxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 175 °C and line a 20 x 20 cm tin with baking paper, letting it hang over the sides.
steps.tip: The overhanging paper lets you lift the whole slab out to cut it.

steps: Put the peanut butter, honey and butter in a pot on low heat and stir until melted and smooth.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the oats, raisins and sunflower seeds until everything is coated.

steps.text: Tip the mix into the tin and press it down very firmly and evenly with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass.
steps.tip: Press hard: this is what stops the bars crumbling.

steps: Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until golden at the edges. Scatter the chocolate chips over the top straight away so they melt a little.

steps.text: Let it cool completely in the tin, then lift it out and cut it into bars.
steps.tip: Use a sharp knife and wait until it is fully cool, or they crumble. They keep a week in a closed tin.

title: Date and cocoa energy balls
description: Blended dates, nuts, oats and cocoa rolled into bite-size balls. No baking, no added sugar.

steps.text: If the dates are hard and dry, soak them in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain them well. Remove any stones.
steps.tip: Soft dates (like Medjool) do not need soaking.

steps: Blend the walnuts and oats in a food processor until finely chopped.

steps.text: Add the dates and cocoa and blend until it clumps together into a sticky dough.
steps.tip: Press a little between your fingers: if it holds together, it is ready. Too dry? Add a spoon of water.

steps.text: Roll the dough into walnut-size balls with your hands, then roll each ball in the coconut.
steps.tip: Slightly wet hands stop the dough sticking.

steps.text: Chill them for an hour to firm up, then keep them in a closed box in the fridge. Two balls make a portion.
steps.tip: They keep about 10 days in the fridge.

title: Peanut butter oat bites
description: Oats, peanut butter, honey, chia and a few chocolate chips rolled into balls. Kids love making them.

steps.text: Put the oats, peanut butter, honey, chia and chocolate chips in a bowl and stir well until it holds together.
steps.tip: Too dry? Add a little more honey or peanut butter. Too sticky? Add a spoon of oats.

steps: Put the bowl in the fridge for 20 minutes so the mix firms up.
Roll it into walnut-size balls with slightly wet hands.

steps.text: Keep them in a closed box in the fridge. Two balls make a portion.
steps.tip: They keep a week in the fridge.

title: Banana oat muffins
description: Soft muffins sweetened mostly with ripe bananas, with oats and a little honey. 12 muffins.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.

steps.text: Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth. Whisk in the eggs, yogurt, honey and oil.
steps.tip: The riper the bananas, the better. Black-spotted bananas make the sweetest muffins.

steps.text: In another bowl mix the oats, flour, baking powder and cinnamon. Tip them into the wet mix and fold with a spatula until just combined.
steps.tip: Stop when you see no dry flour. A lumpy batter makes light muffins; over-mixing makes them tough.

steps: Divide the batter between the cases, filling them almost to the top.

steps.text: Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle of a muffin should come out clean.

steps.text: Let them cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack. Keep in a closed box.
steps.tip: They keep 4 days. You can also freeze them and take one out the night before.

title: Berry yogurt muffins
description: Light muffins with yogurt and frozen berries straight from the freezer. 12 muffins.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
In a large bowl mix the flour, sugar and baking powder.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, yogurt, oil and grated lemon zest.

steps.text: Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir with a spatula just until there is no dry flour left. Fold in the berries straight from the freezer.
steps.tip: Do not thaw the berries first, or they turn the batter purple. A lumpy batter makes light muffins.

steps.text: Fill the cases almost to the top and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden.
steps.tip: A skewer in the middle should come out clean, apart from a little berry juice.

steps.text: Cool them in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
steps.tip: They keep 4 days in a closed box, and freeze well.

title: Homemade hummus with veg sticks
description: Smooth chickpea hummus with tahini, lemon and garlic, with carrot, cucumber and pepper sticks.

steps.text: Drain the chickpeas over a bowl and keep the liquid. Rinse them.
steps.tip: For extra smooth hummus, rub off the skins between your hands. It takes a few minutes but is worth it.

steps: Put the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and {2 tbsp} of the olive oil in a food processor or blender.

steps.text: Blend for 2 to 3 minutes, adding {4 tbsp} of the chickpea liquid a spoon at a time, until very smooth and creamy.
steps.tip: Scrape down the sides a few times. Blending longer than you think is the secret to creamy hummus.

steps: Taste and add more lemon or salt. Spoon it into a bowl, make a swirl with the back of the spoon and drizzle with the rest of the oil.

steps.text: Cut the carrots, cucumber and pepper into sticks and serve with the hummus.
steps.tip: Keep the hummus in a closed box in the fridge for up to 5 days.

title: Beetroot hummus
description: Bright pink hummus with cooked beetroot, chickpeas and tahini. Great on crackers.

steps.text: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Cut the beetroot into chunks.
steps.tip: Beetroot stains, so wear gloves or wash your hands straight away.

steps: Put the beetroot, chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and olive oil in a food processor or blender.
Blend for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth, scraping down the sides. Add a spoon of water if it is too thick.
Taste and add more lemon or salt.

steps.text: Serve with crackers.
steps.tip: It keeps 5 days in a closed box in the fridge.

title: Crunchy roasted chickpeas
description: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with smoked paprika and garlic. A salty snack with lots of protein.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then dry them really well by rolling them in a clean towel.
steps.tip: This is the secret to crunch. Throw away any loose skins that come off.

steps: Toss the chickpeas on a baking tray with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt, and spread them out in one layer.

steps.text: Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, shaking the tray every 10 minutes, until deep golden and crunchy.
steps.tip: Bite one: it should be crisp all the way through. If it is soft in the middle, give them a few more minutes.

steps.text: Let them cool completely on the tray, then keep them in a jar with the lid slightly open.
steps.tip: A closed jar traps moisture and makes them soft. If they soften, crisp them for a few minutes in the oven.

title: Overnight oats jars with berries
description: Four jars of oats soaked in milk and yogurt with chia and berries, ready to grab all week.
steps: Get {4} jars or boxes with lids ready. Divide the oats and chia between them.

steps.text: Whisk the milk, yogurt and honey in a jug and pour it over the oats. Stir well, right to the bottom.
steps.tip: Stir again after a few minutes so the chia seeds do not form clumps.

steps.text: Top with the frozen berries, close the jars and put them in the fridge.
steps.tip: The berries thaw overnight and their juice runs into the oats.

steps.text: They are ready the next morning. Eat them cold, with a splash of milk if they are too thick.
steps.tip: They keep 4 days in the fridge.

title: Apple pie overnight oats
description: Overnight oats with grated apple, cinnamon, peanut butter and raisins. Four jars for the week.

steps.text: Get {4} jars or boxes with lids ready. Wash the apples and grate them coarsely, skin on, into a large bowl.
steps.tip: Grate around the core and stop when you reach the seeds.

steps: Add the oats, cinnamon and raisins and mix so the apple is spread through.
Pour in the milk and kefir and stir well. It looks very runny now, which is right: the oats soak it up overnight.

steps.text: Divide between the jars, put a spoon of peanut butter on top of each, close them and put them in the fridge overnight.
steps.tip: They keep 4 days in the fridge. Eat them cold, or warm one in the microwave.

steps: To eat, stir the peanut butter through. Add a splash of milk if it is too thick.

title: Golden oat flapjacks
description: Buttery, chewy oat squares with honey and a few dried apricots. 16 small pieces.
steps: Heat the oven to 170 °C and line a 20 x 20 cm tin with baking paper. Chop the apricots.
Melt the butter, honey and sugar in a pot on low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Take it off the heat and stir in the oats and apricots until evenly coated.
Tip into the tin and press it down firmly and evenly with the back of a spoon.

steps.text: Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden all over and a little darker at the edges.
steps.tip: They are still soft when they come out and firm up as they cool.

steps.text: Cut into squares while still warm, then let them cool completely in the tin before lifting them out.
steps.tip: Cutting while warm stops them cracking. They keep a week in a closed tin.

title: Oat and raisin cookies
description: Chewy cookies with oats, raisins and cinnamon. Makes about 20.

steps.text: Take the butter out of the fridge early so it is soft. Heat the oven to 180 °C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
steps.tip: Soft butter dents easily when you press it. In a hurry, cut it into small cubes and leave it near the warm oven.

steps: Beat the butter and sugar in a bowl with a wooden spoon or mixer until pale and creamy, then beat in the egg.
Add the flour, oats, baking soda, cinnamon and raisins and mix until no dry bits are left. The dough is thick and sticky.

steps.text: Roll walnut-size balls with your hands, put them on the trays with space between them and flatten each one a little.
steps.tip: They spread in the oven, so leave about 5 cm between them. Wet hands stop the dough sticking.

steps.text: Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle.
steps.tip: They look underdone when you take them out. They firm up as they cool.

steps.text: Leave them on the tray for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack or plate to cool completely. Two cookies make a portion.
steps.tip: They keep a week in a closed tin.

title: Ham and cheese savoury muffins
description: Savoury muffins with ham, cheese, spring onion and a little sweetcorn. Great cold in lunch boxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Dice the ham, grate the cheese, slice the spring onion and drain the sweetcorn.
In a large bowl mix the flour and baking powder. In a jug whisk the eggs, milk and oil.

steps.text: Pour the wet mix into the flour and stir briefly. Fold in the ham, cheese, spring onion and corn until just mixed.
steps.tip: Stop as soon as there is no dry flour. A lumpy batter makes light muffins.

steps.text: Fill the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until risen and golden.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle should come out clean.

steps.text: Cool them on a rack, then keep them in a closed box in the fridge.
steps.tip: They keep 3 days. Warm them for a few seconds in the microwave.

title: Tzatziki with vegetable sticks
description: Thick garlic and cucumber yogurt dip with carrot, pepper and kohlrabi sticks. Make a big box.
steps: Grate the cucumber coarsely, mix it with the salt and leave it in a sieve for 5 minutes.

steps.text: Squeeze the cucumber hard with your hands to get the water out.
steps.tip: This stops the tzatziki going watery.

steps.text: Mix the cucumber with the yogurt, crushed garlic, dill and olive oil. Taste and add salt if needed.
steps.tip: It tastes even better after an hour in the fridge, once the garlic has spread through.

steps: Peel the carrots and kohlrabi and cut them and the pepper into sticks.

steps.text: Keep the sticks in a box of cold water in the fridge and the tzatziki in a closed box.
steps.tip: In water the sticks stay crunchy for days.

title: Homemade trail mix
description: A jar of mixed nuts, seeds, raisins and a few chocolate drops. Portion into 30 g bags.
steps: Put the almonds, walnuts, hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds in a dry frying pan on medium heat.

steps.text: Toast them for 4 minutes, shaking the pan often, until they smell toasty and start to brown.
steps.tip: Tip them out of the pan straight away, or the hot pan keeps cooking them.

steps.text: Spread them on a plate and let them cool completely.
steps.tip: If they are still warm, the chocolate melts.

steps.text: Mix with the raisins and chocolate chips and keep in a jar.
steps.tip: A handful, about 30 g, is a portion.

title: Banana bread
description: Moist loaf made with very ripe bananas, a little sugar and walnuts. Cut into 10 slices.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and line a loaf tin with baking paper. Melt the butter and leave it to cool a little.

steps.text: Mash the bananas in a large bowl with a fork. Mix in the melted butter, sugar and eggs.
steps.tip: The browner the bananas, the sweeter and moister the bread.

steps.text: Chop the walnuts roughly. Add the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and walnuts and fold together until just mixed.
steps.tip: Stop when you see no dry flour. Over-mixing makes it dense.

steps: Pour the batter into the tin and smooth the top.

steps.text: Bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
steps.tip: If the top browns too fast before the middle is done, cover it loosely with foil.

steps.text: Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift it out and let it cool completely before slicing.
steps.tip: Keeps 4 days wrapped. Slices are lovely toasted for breakfast.

title: Carrot and zucchini muffins
description: Lightly sweet muffins hiding grated carrot and zucchini, with oats and cinnamon. 12 muffins.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.

steps.text: Grate the carrots and zucchini. Put the zucchini in a clean towel and squeeze out as much water as you can.
steps.tip: Squeezing matters: wet zucchini makes heavy, damp muffins.

steps: In a large bowl whisk the eggs, oil and honey.
Add the flour, oats, baking powder and cinnamon and stir briefly, then fold in the carrot and zucchini until just mixed.

steps.text: Fill the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden.
steps.tip: A skewer pushed into the middle of a muffin should come out clean.

steps.text: Cool them in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.
steps.tip: They keep 4 days and are good in a lunch box.

title: Seed crackers
description: Thin, crisp crackers made only from seeds, oats and water, baked low and slow. Keep for two weeks.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C. In a bowl mix all the seeds, the oats and the salt with {250 ml} water.
Leave it for 15 minutes, until the chia and flax have soaked up the water and it has turned into a sticky mass.

steps.text: Spread it very thinly on a tray lined with baking paper, using a wet spatula or the back of a wet spoon.
steps.tip: Make it as thin as you can, about 3 mm, without holes. Thin crackers bake crisp all the way through.

steps: Bake for 30 minutes. Take the tray out and cut it into squares with a knife.

steps.text: Pull the squares apart a little and bake for 25 to 30 minutes more, until dry and crisp.
steps.tip: Turn off the oven and leave them inside to cool for extra crunch.

steps.text: Let them cool and keep them in a tin. Serve with the cottage cheese.
steps.tip: They keep two weeks in a closed tin.

title: Smoky paprika popcorn
description: Popcorn popped in a pot with a little oil, tossed with smoked paprika and salt. A big bowl for movie night.

steps.text: Put the oil and {3} popcorn kernels in a large pot with a lid and set it on medium-high heat. Wait until those kernels pop.
steps.tip: When the test kernels pop, the oil is at the right heat. It takes 2 to 3 minutes.

steps.text: Add the rest of the kernels in one layer, put the lid on and take the pot off the heat for 30 seconds.
steps.tip: This short pause warms all the kernels evenly, so more of them pop at the same time.

steps: Put the pot back on the heat. Holding the lid on, shake it gently every few seconds while it pops, about 3 minutes.

steps.text: When there are a few seconds between pops, take the pot off the heat and tip the popcorn into a big bowl.
steps.tip: Do not wait for the last kernels: the popcorn at the bottom burns quickly.

steps.text: Melt the butter and pour it over, then sprinkle with the paprika and salt and toss well. Once cool, keep it in a closed bag or tin.
steps.tip: Without the butter it stays crisp for longer.
